title: Most-watched title per minutes, with names
context: Trending row with titles instead of ids.
task: Return title and minutes = SUM(minutes_watched), top 5 by minutes descending (ties by title).
answer: SELECT s.title, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY s.show_id ORDER BY minutes DESC, s.title LIMIT 5;

title: Completion rate per show
context: How often do viewers finish an episode or film?
task: Return title and completion_pct = completed sessions / all sessions * 100 (1 decimal), for shows with at least 5 sessions.
hint: AVG(completed) * 100 is a neat trick; HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5.
answer: SELECT s.title, ROUND(AVG(w.completed) * 100.0, 1) AS completion_pct FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY s.show_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;

title: Minutes per country
context: Regional engagement.
task: Return country and minutes = SUM(minutes_watched) per user country, ordered by minutes descending (ties by country).
answer: SELECT u.country, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN users u ON u.user_id = w.user_id GROUP BY u.country ORDER BY minutes DESC, u.country;

title: Average rating per genre
context: Which genres do viewers rate highest?
task: Return genre and avg_rating (2 decimals) from ratings joined to shows.
answer: SELECT s.genre, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating FROM ratings r JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = r.show_id GROUP BY s.genre;

title: Never-watched titles
context: Content with zero sessions may be a discovery problem.
task: Return title for shows with no rows in watch_history.
answer: SELECT s.title FROM shows s LEFT JOIN watch_history w ON w.show_id = s.show_id WHERE w.view_id IS NULL;

title: Users who never rated
context: Prompt these users to rate something.
task: Return user_id and email of users with no rows in ratings.
answer: SELECT u.user_id, u.email FROM users u LEFT JOIN ratings r ON r.user_id = u.user_id WHERE r.rating_id IS NULL;

title: Every show with its session count
context: Include shows with zero sessions as 0.
task: Return title and sessions = COUNT(view_id) for every show.
answer: SELECT s.title, COUNT(w.view_id) AS sessions FROM shows s LEFT JOIN watch_history w ON w.show_id = s.show_id GROUP BY s.show_id;

title: Above-average sessions
context: Sessions longer than the overall average.
task: Return view_id and minutes_watched where minutes_watched > the average minutes_watched.
answer: SELECT view_id, minutes_watched FROM watch_history WHERE minutes_watched > (SELECT AVG(minutes_watched) FROM watch_history);

title: Users who watched Squid Game
context: Audience list for a sequel campaign.
task: Return DISTINCT email of users with a session on the show titled 'Squid Game'.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT u.email FROM users u WHERE u.user_id IN (SELECT w.user_id FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id WHERE s.title = 'Squid Game');

title: Users who watched a Documentary
context: Documentary fans for a new release push.
task: Return user_id for users with at least one session on a show in the 'Documentary' genre.
answer: SELECT u.user_id FROM users u WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id WHERE w.user_id = u.user_id AND s.genre = 'Documentary');

title: Premium users who never used a TV
context: Premium includes 4K — but some never watch on TV.
task: Return user_id for users whose plan is 'Premium' and who have no session with device 'TV'.
answer: SELECT u.user_id FROM users u WHERE u.plan = 'Premium' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM watch_history w WHERE w.user_id = u.user_id AND w.device = 'TV');

title: Device split per user
context: Wide format: minutes on TV vs Mobile per user.
task: Return user_id, tv_minutes and mobile_minutes (sums of minutes_watched by device) for every user with sessions.
hint: SUM(CASE WHEN device = 'TV' THEN minutes_watched ELSE 0 END).
answer: SELECT user_id, SUM(CASE WHEN device = 'TV' THEN minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) AS tv_minutes, SUM(CASE WHEN device = 'Mobile' THEN minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) AS mobile_minutes FROM watch_history GROUP BY user_id;

title: Series vs movie minutes per country
context: Do some markets prefer films?
task: Return country, series_minutes and movie_minutes per user country.
hint: Join users and shows; conditional SUM on type.
answer: SELECT u.country, SUM(CASE WHEN s.type = 'Series' THEN w.minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) AS series_minutes, SUM(CASE WHEN s.type = 'Movie' THEN w.minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) AS movie_minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN users u ON u.user_id = w.user_id JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY u.country;

title: Monthly minutes
context: The engagement chart.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM) and minutes = SUM(minutes_watched), ordered by month.
answer: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', watch_date) AS month, SUM(minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

title: Weekend share of viewing
context: Is viewing a weekend habit?
task: Return weekend_pct = minutes on Saturday/Sunday divided by all minutes * 100, 1 decimal.
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%w', watch_date) IN ('0','6') THEN minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(minutes_watched), 1) AS weekend_pct FROM watch_history;

title: Days from signup to first watch
context: Activation speed per user.
task: Return user_id and days_to_first_watch = days between signup_date and the user's earliest watch_date (integer).
answer: SELECT u.user_id, CAST(julianday(MIN(w.watch_date)) - julianday(u.signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_to_first_watch FROM users u JOIN watch_history w ON w.user_id = u.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id;

title: Subscription length in days
context: How long did cancelled subscriptions last?
task: Return subscription_id and days_active = end_date minus start_date in days (integer) for subscriptions with status 'cancelled'.
answer: SELECT subscription_id, CAST(julianday(end_date) - julianday(start_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_active FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'cancelled';

title: Users who watched the same show on the same day twice or more
context: Repeat plays of the same title in one day hint at binge or rewatch.
task: Return DISTINCT user_id, show_id and watch_date where the user has 2+ sessions of that show on that date.
hint: GROUP BY user_id, show_id, watch_date HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2.
answer: SELECT user_id, show_id, watch_date FROM watch_history GROUP BY user_id, show_id, watch_date HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

title: Rated but never watched
context: Data-quality check: ratings for shows the user has no session on.
task: Return DISTINCT (user_id, show_id) pairs present in ratings but not in watch_history.
answer: SELECT user_id, show_id FROM ratings EXCEPT SELECT user_id, show_id FROM watch_history;

title: Content origins and user countries
context: One list of every country that appears as a content origin OR a user country.
task: Return one column country with the union (no duplicates) of shows.origin_country and users.country.
answer: SELECT origin_country AS country FROM shows UNION SELECT country FROM users;

title: Share of minutes by genre
context: Pie chart of engagement by genre.
task: Using a CTE, return genre and share_pct = genre minutes / total minutes * 100 (1 decimal).
hint: WITH g AS (...) then divide by (SELECT SUM(minutes) FROM g).
answer: WITH g AS (SELECT s.genre, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY s.genre) SELECT genre, ROUND(minutes * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(minutes) FROM g), 1) AS share_pct FROM g;

title: Churn rate by plan
context: Which plan loses the most subscribers?
task: Return plan and churn_pct = cancelled subscriptions / all subscriptions of that plan * 100 (1 decimal).
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT plan, COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled FROM subscriptions GROUP BY plan) SELECT plan, ROUND(cancelled * 100.0 / total, 1) AS churn_pct FROM t;

title: Shows loved and finished
context: Titles with an average rating of at least 4 AND at least 3 ratings.
task: Return title, avg_rating (2 decimals) and rating_count for shows with avg rating >= 4 and 3+ ratings.
answer: SELECT s.title, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating, COUNT(*) AS rating_count FROM ratings r JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = r.show_id GROUP BY s.show_id HAVING AVG(r.rating) >= 4 AND COUNT(*) >= 3;

title: Multi-genre viewers
context: Users who watched 4 or more distinct genres.
task: Return user_id and genres = COUNT(DISTINCT genre) for users with 4+ distinct genres watched.
answer: SELECT w.user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s.genre) AS genres FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY w.user_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.genre) >= 4;

title: Users above the average minutes
context: Power viewers.
task: Return user_id and total_minutes for users whose total exceeds the average total per user.
hint: Derived table of totals, compared to AVG of another derived table.
answer: SELECT user_id, total_minutes FROM (SELECT user_id, SUM(minutes_watched) AS total_minutes FROM watch_history GROUP BY user_id) t WHERE total_minutes > (SELECT AVG(m) FROM (SELECT SUM(minutes_watched) AS m FROM watch_history GROUP BY user_id));

title: What Premium users in India watch
context: Regional premium content strategy.
task: Return DISTINCT title for shows watched by users with country 'India' and plan 'Premium'.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT s.title FROM users u JOIN watch_history w ON w.user_id = u.user_id JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id WHERE u.country = 'India' AND u.plan = 'Premium';

title: Local content share per country
context: How much of a country's viewing is content made in that country?
task: Return country and local_pct = minutes on shows whose origin_country equals the user's country / all minutes * 100 (1 decimal).
answer: SELECT u.country, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.origin_country = u.country THEN w.minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(w.minutes_watched), 1) AS local_pct FROM watch_history w JOIN users u ON u.user_id = w.user_id JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY u.country;

title: Monthly recurring revenue
context: MRR = sum of monthly_price over active subscriptions.
task: Return mrr = SUM(monthly_price) for subscriptions with status 'active', 2 decimals.
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(monthly_price), 2) AS mrr FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'active';

title: Lifetime revenue per subscription
context: Approximate revenue = months × price.
task: Return subscription_id and revenue = ROUND(monthly_price * (days between start_date and COALESCE(end_date, '2025-07-31')) / 30.0, 2).
hint: COALESCE the open end date to '2025-07-31'.
answer: SELECT subscription_id, ROUND(monthly_price * (julianday(COALESCE(end_date, '2025-07-31')) - julianday(start_date)) / 30.0, 2) AS revenue FROM subscriptions;

title: Subscription end or 'ongoing'
context: Report-friendly end column.
task: Return subscription_id and ends = COALESCE(end_date, 'ongoing').
answer: SELECT subscription_id, COALESCE(end_date, 'ongoing') AS ends FROM subscriptions;

title: Sessions longer than the title's runtime
context: minutes_watched should never exceed duration_min.
task: Return view_id, minutes_watched and duration_min where minutes_watched > duration_min.
answer: SELECT w.view_id, w.minutes_watched, s.duration_min FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id WHERE w.minutes_watched > s.duration_min;

title: Sessions before signup
context: A session dated before the user's signup is impossible.
task: Return view_id, user_id and watch_date for sessions where watch_date < the user's signup_date.
hint: Join users; compare dates as text.
answer: SELECT w.view_id, w.user_id, w.watch_date FROM watch_history w JOIN users u ON u.user_id = w.user_id WHERE w.watch_date < u.signup_date;

title: Users who ever upgraded
context: Upsell success.
task: Return DISTINCT user_id from subscriptions where status is 'upgraded'.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'upgraded';
